mainTopic: Agents who take a deal for themselves, the rule of עני המהפך בחררה, and whether a woman can back out of a betrothal set to take effect after thirty days.
overview: The גמרא first explains why our משנה says 'his friend' (חבירו) while an earlier משנה says 'his agent' (שלוחו): each wording teaches the bigger חידוש. Next come two stories. In one, רבין חסידא was sent to betroth a woman for his son and betrothed her himself. In the other, רב was sent to buy land for רבה בר בר חנה and bought it for himself. In each story the גמרא asks how a great man could act with what the ברייתא calls מנהג רמאות. It answers that the sender could never have gotten the deal, and that there was no time to tell him first. Then רבי אבא buys a field רב גידל was negotiating for, and the rule of עני המהפך בחררה, that whoever takes it is called a רשע, leads to the field becoming 'the land of the רבנן.' The גמרא then returns to the משנה about a betrothal that takes effect after thirty days. רב and שמואל rule that it works even if the money was spent. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue whether the woman can change her mind before then, and they trade challenges from the laws of תרומה, גט and the טומאה of vessels; that last challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does the other משנה say 'his agent'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the earlier משנה uses the word 'his agent' when our משנה uses 'his friend'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different there, that the משנה teaches 'one who says to his agent'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question about word choice. Our משנה says 'his friend' (חבירו), but the earlier משנה says 'his agent' (שלוחו), so why the difference?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both משניות describe the same basic situation: a man sends someone to betroth a woman for him. Since the cases look alike, the גמרא expects the same word in both. It wants to know what each wording is meant to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? A question asking why two similar cases are treated or worded differently
There, meaning in the other משנה
His agent, someone officially appointed to act for him

phrases.english: And what is different there
phrases.notes: 'There' is the earlier משנה about someone sent to betroth a woman in a specific place.

phrases.english: that it teaches 'one who says to his agent'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the question, begun before this section, about why our משנה uses חבירו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the two משניות use different words for the person sent to betroth.

steps.title: Our משנה says 'his friend' to teach the bigger חידוש
steps.stepSummary: Each משנה picked the word that teaches the bigger חידוש. Here, saying 'friend' teaches that even a non-agent who takes the woman is called a רמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it teaches a חידוש, and there it teaches a חידוש. Here it teaches a חידוש: if it had said 'his agent', I would have thought only an agent is called a רמאי, because the sender relies on him and thinks, 'He will do my errand.' But a friend, whom he does not rely on, I might say is not a רמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both word choices were chosen on purpose. It explains our משנה first: the word 'friend' shows that even a person who is not an official agent is called a רמאי if he betroths the woman for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an official agent, the sender fully trusts him, so betraying that trust is obviously רמאות. With just a friend, the trust is weaker, so we might have excused him. By saying 'friend', the משנה teaches the stronger point, and the agent case is then obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: A חידוש; the bigger or more surprising lesson
I would have thought (the wrong first assumption)
He relies on him; he trusts him

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the betrothal works, since our case says it does. The question is only whether the man who took her is called a רמאי.

phrases.english: Here it teaches us a bigger lesson,
and there it teaches us a bigger lesson.
Here it teaches us a bigger lesson:
for if it had taught 'his agent', I would have thought:
it is his agent who is a cheat,
because he relies on him, thinking:
'He will carry out my errand for me,'
but his friend, whom he does not rely on,
I might say he is not a cheat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא רְבוּתָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, וְהָתָם רְבוּתָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the word-choice question, starting with our משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each wording teaches the larger חידוש for its own case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a trusted official agent is called a רמאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a friend who was not an official agent is called a רמאי.

steps.title: The other משנה says 'his agent' to teach the bigger חידוש
steps.stepSummary: The earlier משנה says 'agent' to teach that even an official agent cannot betroth the woman in a different place than he was told.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it teaches a חידוש: if it had said 'his friend', I would have thought only a friend's betrothal in another place fails, since the sender assumed the friend would not go to any trouble. But an agent, who does go to trouble, I might say was only being shown where she is likely to be. So it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the other משנה: the word 'agent' shows that even an official agent must stick to the place he was told.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a friend, we could understand that the sender meant 'only in that place', since a friend would not search around. An agent is expected to make an effort, so we might think naming the place was just a helpful hint. The משנה says 'agent' to teach that even then, the betrothal elsewhere does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Just pointing out a place; a hint, not a condition

steps.whatToRemember: Each משנה uses the word that teaches the bigger point. Our משנה says 'friend': even a non-agent who takes the woman is a רמאי. The other משנה says 'agent': even an official agent cannot betroth her in a different place.

phrases.english: There it teaches us a bigger lesson:
for if it had taught 'one who says to his friend', I would have thought:

phrases.aramaic: חֲבֵירוֹ הוּא דְּכִי קִדְּשָׁהּ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר
phrases.english: it is a friend who, when he betrothed her in another place,
she is not betrothed, because the sender thinks: 'He will not go to trouble,'
but his agent, who does go to trouble,
I might say: he was only showing him a place,
phrases.notes: He means the place was just a tip about where to find her, not a strict condition.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer by explaining the other משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each wording teaches the larger חידוש for its own case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For an agent, naming the place was just a hint.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even an agent's betrothal in another place does not work.

steps.title: רבין חסידא betroths his son's match for himself
steps.stepSummary: A story: רבין חסידא went to betroth a woman for his son, but betrothed her to himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין the Pious went to betroth a woman for his son, and he betrothed her to himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that looks exactly like our משנה's case. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man is called חסידא, 'the pious one', yet he seems to have done just what the ברייתא calls רמאות. That clash is what drives the next steps.

phrases.english: Ravin the Pious went
to betroth a woman for his son,
and he betrothed her to himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִין חֲסִידָא אֲזַיל לְקַדּוֹשֵׁי לֵיהּ אִיתְּתָא לִבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from word choice to a real-life story about the same law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבין חסידא, sent for his son, betrothed the woman himself.

steps.title: But the ברייתא calls this רמאות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story: the ברייתא says doing this is deceitful, so how could a pious man do it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: What he did is done, but he acted toward him in a deceitful way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the story. The ברייתא says the betrothal works but the man acted like a cheat, so how could רבין, a חסיד, act that way?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is not about whether the betrothal works, since the ברייתא agrees that it does. It is about behavior: a pious man should not do something labeled רמאות.

keyTerms.meaning: What he did is done; the act is valid

phrases.english: But it was taught: What he did is done,
except that he treated him in a deceitful way!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the story from step 4 using the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא labels this act רמאות, and a חסיד would not act deceitfully.

steps.title: They would not give her to the son
steps.stepSummary: The woman's family refused to give her to the son, so רבין did not take anything away from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would not give her to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the family refused to let the son marry her. So רבין did not steal his son's match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמאות means taking something the sender could have had. Here the son never had a chance, so marrying her himself did not cost the son anything.

phrases.english: They would not give her to him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the son: her family refused that match.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different facts: the son could never have married her.
steps.terutzMaskana: The son had no chance, so there was no רמאות.

steps.title: He should have told his son first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: even so, he should have told his son before betrothing her himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should have let him know!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again: even if the family refused the son, רבין should have gone back and told his son first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer explains why it was not stealing. But acting without telling the son still seems improper, so the גמרא asks why רבין did not report back first.

keyTerms.meaning: To inform; to let him know

phrases.english: He should have informed him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conduct again, even after the answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבין acting without telling his son
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Proper conduct would be to report the refusal to the son before acting.

steps.title: Someone else might have taken her in the meantime
steps.stepSummary: רבין worried that while he went to tell his son, another man would come and betroth her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought: in the meantime, someone else will come and betroth her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבין was afraid of losing the match. If he went to tell his son, someone else might betroth her in the meantime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Waiting would not have helped the son, who was refused anyway, and could have made רבין lose her too. So acting right away was reasonable and not deceitful.
steps.whatToRemember: רבין חסידא was not a רמאי: the family refused his son, and stopping to report back could have let someone else betroth her.

phrases.english: He thought: in the meantime
another person will come and betroth her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He should have waited and informed his son.
steps.terutzMaskana: Waiting risked losing her to another man, so acting at once was proper.

steps.title: רב buys land for himself instead of for רבה בר בר חנה
steps.stepSummary: A second story like רבין's: רבה בר בר חנה gave רב money to buy land for him, but רב bought it for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה gave money to רב and said: Buy this land for me. רב went and bought it for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story that matches the story of רבין חסידא. An agent was sent to buy something for someone else and took it for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same problem we just saw, now with buying land instead of betrothing a woman. The reader should expect the same questions that were asked about רבין.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה יְהַיב לֵיהּ זוּזֵי לְרַב,
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana gave money to Rav,
he said: Buy this land for me.
He went and bought it for himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה יְהַיב לֵיהּ זוּזֵי לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to רבין חסידא (step 4), now about buying land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story: an agent sent to buy land for someone bought it for himself.

steps.title: The ברייתא calls this deceitful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב with the same ברייתא: an agent who does this has acted deceitfully.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: What he did is done, but he acted toward him in a deceitful way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how a great man like רב could do something the ברייתא calls deceitful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the purchase still works legally, but it is wrong behavior. So the question is not about the law of the sale. It is about how רב could act this way.

keyTerms.meaning: What he did is done (it works legally)

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
phrases.notes: This is the same ברייתא the גמרא used against רבין in step 5.

phrases.english: What he did is done,
but he treated him in a deceitful way!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the story in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's behavior in buying the land for himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls such an agent deceitful, and רב would not act deceitfully.

steps.title: The sellers would only sell to רב
steps.stepSummary: The land was in a valley of violent men who respected רב but not רבה בר בר חנה, so רבה בר בר חנה could never have gotten it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The land was in a valley of violent men. They showed respect to רב, but they did not show respect to רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רבה בר בר חנה could never have bought this land anyway, so רב took nothing away from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same idea as the answer about רבין (step 6). Deceit means taking away something the other person could have had. Here the sellers would only deal with רב, so no one lost anything.

phrases.english: It was in a valley of violent men,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: to Rav they showed respect,

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה – לָא נָהֲגִי בֵּיהּ כָּבוֹד.
phrases.english: to Rabba bar bar Chana they did not show respect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: the sender could never have gotten the item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב took a deal away from רבה בר בר חנה, which is deceit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sellers would never have sold to רבה בר בר חנה, so רב took nothing from him.

steps.title: רב should have told him first
steps.stepSummary: Even so, רב should have told רבה בר בר חנה before buying it for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should have informed him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again, just as it did with רבין: רב should have let רבה בר בר חנה know first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if רבה בר בר חנה could not buy the land, being open and honest is still expected. The challenge is about the missing step of telling him.

phrases.english: He should have informed him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the answer in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's failure to tell רבה בר בר חנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even with no loss, honesty requires telling the sender before buying for yourself.

steps.title: Someone else might have bought it in the meantime
steps.stepSummary: רב worried that while he went to tell רבה בר בר חנה, another person would buy the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought: in the meantime, another person will come and buy it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there was no time. Telling him first could have meant losing the land completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the answer about רבין (step 8). Acting fast was needed so the land would not go to a stranger.
steps.whatToRemember: An agent who takes the deal for himself is called deceitful. It is allowed only if the sender could never have gotten it, and if there was no time to tell him.

phrases.english: He thought: in the meantime
another person will come and buy it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב had time to tell him and did not.
steps.terutzMaskana: Waiting would have risked losing the land to a stranger.

steps.title: רבי אבא buys the field רב גידל was trying to get
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל was working on getting a field, and רבי אבא bought it. The complaint went up to רב יצחק נפחא, who said to wait until רבי אבא came for the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל was negotiating for a certain field. רבי אבא went and bought it. רב גידל complained to רבי זירא, and רבי זירא complained to רב יצחק נפחא. He said: Wait until he comes up to us for the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about one person stepping in on another person's deal. This step sets up the scene for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי אבא was not anyone's agent. He was an outsider who bought a field someone else was already working on. That makes it a new kind of case.

keyTerms.meaning: Negotiating, working on getting something (literally, turning over)

phrases.aramaic: רַב גִּידֵּל הֲוָה מְהַפֵּיךְ בְּהַהִיא אַרְעָא.
phrases.english: Rav Giddel was negotiating for a certain field.
Rabbi Abba went and bought it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל רַב גִּידֵּל קַבְלֵיהּ לְרַבִּי זֵירָא.
phrases.english: Rav Giddel went and complained to Rabbi Zeira.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל רַבִּי זֵירָא וְקַבְלֵיהּ לְרַב יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira went and complained to Rav Yitzchak Nappacha.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: הַמְתֵּן עַד שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה אֶצְלֵנוּ לָרֶגֶל.
phrases.english: He said to him: Wait until he comes up to us for the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב גִּידֵּל הֲוָה מְהַפֵּיךְ בְּהַהִיא אַרְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the agent stories to a new story about an outsider stepping in on someone's deal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: רבי אבא bought a field רב גידל was negotiating for.

steps.title: The case of the poor man and the loaf
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק נפחא asks רבי אבא about a poor man going after a loaf of bread when someone else comes and takes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came up, he found him and said to him: A poor man is going after a cake of bread, and another person comes and takes it from him. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק נפחא does not accuse רבי אבא directly. He asks a general question first, to get רבי אבא to state the rule himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The poor man and the loaf are a picture of רב גידל and the field. Whatever רבי אבא answers will apply to what he himself did.

keyTerms.meaning: A poor man going after a loaf (the name of this הלכה)
A small loaf or cake of bread

phrases.english: When he came up, he found him,
he said to him: A poor man is going after a loaf,
and another came and took it from him, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: עָנִי מְהַפֵּךְ בַּחֲרָרָה, וּבָא אַחֵר וּנְטָלָהּ הֵימֶנּוּ, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The meeting planned in step 14 happens.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the law when someone takes what another person was already trying to get?

steps.title: The one who takes it is called wicked
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that the person who took it is called a רשע.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He is called wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא states the rule: whoever steps in and takes what someone else was working on is called a רשע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking it is not legally stealing, but it is strongly condemned. With this answer, רבי אבא has set up the challenge against himself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known הלכה of עני המהפך בחררה: do not step in on a deal someone else is already making.

phrases.english: He said to him: He is called wicked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The one who takes it is called a רשע.

steps.title: Then why did you do it?
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק נפחא turns the rule back on רבי אבא: why did you buy the field רב גידל was working on?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why did the master act this way?
steps.whatsHappening: Now רב יצחק נפחא shows that the question was about רבי אבא himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא just said that taking someone's deal makes you a רשע. Yet he did exactly that with רב גידל's field.

keyTerms.meaning: The master (a respectful way to say 'you')

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא מָר מַאי טַעְמָא עֲבַד הָכִי?
phrases.english: But then, why did the master act this way?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא מָר מַאי טַעְמָא עֲבַד הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי אבא's own answer in step 16 against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's purchase of the field
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By his own rule, buying the field רב גידל was negotiating for makes him a רשע.

steps.title: Rabbi Abba did not know
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that he did not know רב גידל was negotiating for the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I did not know.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא defends himself: he had no idea someone else was already working on this deal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is about someone who knowingly steps in. Since רבי אבא did not know, he did not act wickedly.

phrases.english: He said to him: I did not know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אבא knowingly took רב גידל's deal.
steps.terutzMaskana: He did not know, so he is not a רשע.

steps.title: Now that you know, give it to him
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק נפחא says: now that you know, give the field to רב גידל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now too, let the master give it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק נפחא accepts that רבי אבא did not know, but pushes further: now that he knows, he should hand the field over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not knowing explains why he bought it. It does not explain why he should keep it now that he knows.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him give it to him

phrases.english: Now too, let the master give it to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the answer in step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once he knows, keeping the field is the same as knowingly taking it.

steps.title: Not for sale, but he may take it as a gift
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא will not sell it, because selling your first field is a bad sign. He offers it to רב גידל as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I will not sell it, because it is the first land I bought, and that is not a good sign. If he wants it as a gift, let him take it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא agrees to let רב גידל have the field, but only as a gift, not as a sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He has a reason not to sell: selling the first field you ever bought is a bad sign. A gift lets him fix the wrong without selling.

keyTerms.meaning: Sell it, I will not sell it
It is not a good sign

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זַבּוֹנֵי לָא מְזַבֵּינְנָא לַהּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: As for selling, I will not sell it,
because it is the first land,
phrases.notes: He means the first field he ever bought.

phrases.english: and the thing is not a good sign.
If he wants it as a gift, let him take it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the demand in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial agreement with a different method
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He must sell the field back to רב גידל.
steps.terutzMaskana: He will not sell, because it is a bad sign, but he offers it as a gift.

steps.title: Neither rabbi uses the field, and it becomes the land of the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל will not take a gift, and רבי אבא will not use a field רב גידל had been working on. So the field was left for the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל did not go down to it, as it is written: 'And one who hates gifts will live.' רבי אבא did not go down to it, because רב גידל had been negotiating for it. Neither one went down to it, and it was called 'the land of the רבנן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: both rabbis keep away from the field for their own reasons, and it becomes known as the land of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב גידל avoids gifts because of the פסוק in משלי. רבי אבא avoids the field because of the rule of עני המהפך בחררה. Since both refused it, the field ended up for the use of the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Went down to it (took it and used it)
One who hates gifts will live

steps.whatToRemember: Someone who steps in on another person's deal is called a רשע (עני המהפך בחררה). These rabbis were so careful that neither would use the field.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel did not go down to it,
phrases.notes: 'Go down to' a field means to take it and use it.

phrases.english: as it is written: "And one who hates gifts will live."
Rabbi Abba did not go down to it
because Rav Giddel had been negotiating for it.

phrases.aramaic: לָא מָר נָחֵית לַהּ וְלָא מָר נָחֵית לַהּ
phrases.english: Neither this master went down to it nor that master went down to it,
and it was called "the land of the Rabbis."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב גִּידֵּל לָא נָחֵית לַהּ, דִּכְתִיב: וְשׂוֹנֵא מַתָּנֹת יִחְיֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells what happened after the gift offer in step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Neither rabbi took the field. רב גידל avoided gifts, and רבי אבא avoided taking another person's deal. So it became 'the land of the רבנן.'

steps.title: What if no one else betrothed her within the thirty days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about betrothal 'after thirty days' and asks what the law is if no other man came along during that time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And similarly, one who says to a woman, Be betrothed to me after thirty days, and another man betrothed her in the meantime, she belongs to the second man.' Now the גמרא asks: if no other man came and betrothed her within the thirty days, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה and asking a question about it. This sets up the answer of רב and שמואל in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only discussed the case where a second man stepped in. Here the גמרא asks about the ordinary case where nobody interferes. The real concern, as the next step shows, is that the money might be spent before the thirty days are over.

keyTerms.meaning: Be betrothed to me: the wording a man uses to make קידושין
Thirty (days): the waiting period before the betrothal takes effect
What is the law? (a standard way of asking a question)

phrases.english: And similarly, one who says to a woman
'Be betrothed to me' etc.
phrases.notes: כו׳ means 'etc.' The משנה continues: 'after thirty days,' and if another man betrothed her in the meantime, she is his.

phrases.english: If another man did not come and betroth her
within the thirty days, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא בָּא אַחֵר וְקִידְּשָׁה בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of רבי אבא and רב גידל and goes back to the משנה to begin a new discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the delayed betrothal take effect after thirty days when no one else interfered?

steps.title: She is betrothed, even if the money was spent
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל both rule that she is betrothed after thirty days, even if the betrothal money was used up before then.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both say: she is betrothed, even if the money was used up.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל answer the question: the betrothal takes effect after thirty days. This is true even if the coins are gone by then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that because the money no longer exists when the thirty days end, nothing is there to make the קידושין work. רב and שמואל say the betrothal still takes effect. The next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Were used up or spent (literally, 'were eaten up')

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel both say:
She is betrothed,
even if the money has been used up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is betrothed after thirty days, even if the money was spent before then.

steps.title: Why does the betrothal work if the money is gone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ruling of רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב and שמואל rule this way. This sets up the explanation in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the coins being spent before the betrothal takes effect. The גמרא wants to know how a betrothal can work when, at that moment, the money is gone.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind ruling that the betrothal works even though the money was spent.

steps.title: The coins are neither a loan nor a deposit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the betrothal coins are not like a מלוה and not like a פקדון.
steps.simpleTranslation: These coins are not like a loan, and they are not like a deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the main answer in short form: these coins don't fit either of two categories that would cause a problem. The next two steps explain each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a מלוה or a lost פקדון, there would be a problem using the money for קידושין. By saying the coins are like neither one, the גמרא shows why spending them does not cancel the betrothal.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit: something left with someone to watch
Are similar to, are comparable to

phrases.english: These coins are not comparable to a loan
and are not comparable to a deposit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי זוּזֵי לָא לְמִלְוָה דָּמוּ וְלָא לְפִקָּדוֹן דָּמוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'why' question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The betrothal coins are in their own category: neither a loan nor a deposit.

steps.title: Why the coins are not like a deposit
steps.stepSummary: A lost deposit is the owner's loss, but these coins are lost while they belong to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are not like a deposit. A deposit gets used up while it still belongs to its owner, but these coins get used up while they belong to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of its answer: why the coins are not like a פקדון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a פקדון is lost, the owner loses it, so the person watching it never really owned it. The betrothal coins were given to the woman as hers. So if they are spent, she is the one who spent her own money, and the gift to her still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: In its owner's possession (the owner bears the loss)

phrases.english: They are not comparable to a deposit:
a deposit is used up in its owner's possession,
phrases.notes: He means that if a deposit is lost, the loss belongs to the owner, not to the person watching it.

phrases.english: but these are used up in her own possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the deposit half of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The coins belong to her, so if they are lost, it is her loss, unlike a deposit.

steps.title: Why the coins are not like a loan
steps.stepSummary: A loan is given to be spent, but these coins were given from the start for קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are also not like a loan. A loan is given in order to be spent, but these coins were given to her as betrothal money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of its answer: why the coins are not like a מלוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loan money is meant to be spent, so nothing of value is in her hands for the betrothal. These coins were handed over from the start for the purpose of קידושין. So even if she later spends them, they were real betrothal money.

keyTerms.meaning: As betrothal money, for the purpose of קידושין

steps.whatToRemember: Betrothal coins given for a delayed קידושין are neither a פקדון (her loss, not his) nor a מלוה (given as betrothal money, not to be spent). So she is betrothed after thirty days even if the coins were used up.

phrases.english: They are also not comparable to a loan:
a loan is given to be spent,
these, as betrothal money
he gave them to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the loan half of step 25 and completes the reasoning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The coins were given as betrothal money from the start, not to be spent like a loan.

steps.title: Can she change her mind before the thirty days end?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if no other man betrothed her, but she herself backed out before the thirty days ended, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: If another man did not come and betroth her, but she changed her mind, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second new question about the waiting period. This sets up an argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first question was about the money. This question is about her agreement. Since the betrothal only takes effect after thirty days, can she take back her 'yes' before then?

keyTerms.meaning: She changed her mind, took back her agreement

phrases.english: If another man did not come and betroth her,
and she changed her mind, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא בָּא אַחֵר וְקִידְּשָׁהּ, וְחָזְרָה בָּהּ, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question about the same משנה case, now about her backing out instead of the money.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can the woman take back her agreement before the delayed betrothal takes effect?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: she can change her mind
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says she can back out, because a new statement can cancel an earlier statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: she can change her mind, because one statement can come and cancel another statement.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that she may back out before the thirty days end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her agreement was only words, and the betrothal has not taken effect yet. רבי יוחנן holds that her later words ('I don't want this anymore') can cancel her earlier words ('I agree').

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: She can retract,
a statement comes and cancels a statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She can retract; a later statement cancels an earlier one.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: she cannot change her mind
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש disagrees and says she cannot back out, because a new statement cannot cancel an earlier statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: she cannot change her mind, because one statement cannot come and cancel another statement.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the opposite answer: her agreement stands, and she cannot take it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the betrothal has not taken effect yet. They argue about whether words can undo earlier words. ריש לקיש holds they cannot, so her original agreement still holds and the betrothal takes effect after thirty days.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think ריש לקיש means she is already betrothed now. The betrothal still only takes effect after thirty days. He just means her second statement does not cancel her first.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: She cannot retract,
a statement does not come and cancel a statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוחנן in step 29 and answers the same question the opposite way.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She cannot retract; a later statement does not cancel an earlier one.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges from canceling a messenger for תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a משנה. If an owner cancels his messenger before the messenger separates תרומה, the separation does not count. This shows that words can cancel words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: If the owner canceled the messenger before he separated תרומה, his תרומה is not תרומה. Here we have one statement and then another statement, and the second statement cancels the first!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's view with a case from the laws of תרומה. In that case, a later statement clearly cancels an earlier one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner appointed the messenger with words, and he canceled him with words. The משנה says the cancellation works, so the messenger's תרומה does not count. That looks exactly like 'a statement cancels a statement,' which is what ריש לקיש denied.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
If he canceled,
phrases.notes: The case: an owner appointed a messenger to separate תרומה for him, and then called it off.

phrases.english: if he canceled before [the messenger] separated תרומה,
his תרומה is not תרומה.
But here it is a statement and a statement,
and a statement comes and cancels a statement!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's position from step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that a statement cannot cancel a statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Appointing and canceling a messenger are both just words, and the משנה says the cancellation works.

steps.title: Giving money to a woman counts as an action
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that קידושין money placed in the woman's hand is like an action. Words can cancel words, but words cannot cancel an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: Giving money into a woman's hand is different. It is like an action, and a statement cannot come and cancel an action.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends himself by showing how our case of קידושין is different from the תרומה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the תרומה case, nothing physical happened yet. There was only talk on both sides, so the cancellation works. In our case, the coins were actually handed to her, and that is an action. A later statement cannot undo an action.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's rule: words can cancel words, but words cannot cancel an action. Handing over money counts as an action.

phrases.english: Giving money into a woman's hand is different,
because it is like an action,
and a statement does not come and cancel an action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our case is just like תרומה, with words on both sides.
steps.terutzMaskana: Handing money to the woman is an action, which words cannot cancel.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges from canceling a גט held by a messenger
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a ברייתא. A husband can cancel a גט that he already handed to a messenger. Handing something to a messenger should be like handing money to a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him again: One who sends a גט to his wife, and then catches up with the messenger, or sends another messenger after him, and says, 'The גט I gave you is canceled' — it is canceled. But giving a גט into a messenger's hand is like giving money into a woman's hand, and still it teaches that it is canceled!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a second challenge. Here something physical was handed over, and words still canceled it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש just said that a physical handing-over is an action, and words cannot cancel an action. But the husband physically handed the גט to the messenger, and the ברייתא says his later words cancel it. So it seems words can cancel even a handing-over.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: This is still רבי יוחנן challenging ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: One who sends a גט to his wife
and he caught up with the messenger

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁלַח אַחֲרָיו שָׁלִיחַ וְאָמַר לוֹ:
phrases.english: or sent a messenger after him and said to him:
"The גט that I gave you is canceled"
it is canceled.
But giving a גט into a messenger's hand

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי נְתִינַת מָעוֹת לְיַד אִשָּׁה דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: is like giving money into a woman's hand,
and yet it teaches that it is canceled!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction ריש לקיש made in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that a physical handing-over cannot be canceled by words
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Handing a גט to a messenger is a physical handing-over, yet words cancel it.

steps.title: Until the גט reaches her, it is only words
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that handing the גט to the messenger does not count as the real action. Only when it reaches the wife is there an action, so until then, words can cancel words.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, as long as the גט has not reached her hand, it is a statement and a statement, so a statement comes and cancels a statement.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the גט challenge by saying it really is a case of words against words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The action that matters for divorce is the גט arriving in the wife's hand. Giving it to the messenger is just part of the appointment, which is words. So canceling it before it reaches her is words canceling words. That fits ריש לקיש's rule.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two handings-over. Coins handed to the woman herself count as an action. A גט handed only to a messenger does not count as the action yet.

phrases.english: There too,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל כַּמָּה דְּלָא מְטָא גִּיטָּא לִידַהּ –
phrases.english: as long as the גט has not reached her hand,
it is a statement and a statement,
so a statement comes and cancels a statement.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי, כֹּל כַּמָּה דְּלָא מְטָא גִּיטָּא לִידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (no real action yet)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Handing the גט to the messenger is like handing money to the woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the גט reaching the wife is an action. Before that, it is all words.

steps.title: ריש לקיש challenges from the טומאה of vessels
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש now challenges רבי יוחנן. He brings the rule that a vessel can become able to receive טומאה through thought alone, but it can only leave its טומאה status through a physical change.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש challenged רבי יוחנן: All vessels go down into their טומאה through thought, but they do not come up out of their טומאה except through a change made by an action.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the other side attacks. ריש לקיש quotes a rule about vessels to challenge רבי יוחנן. This step sets up the challenge, and the גמרא will spell out how it applies next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A craftsman's thought alone, deciding the vessel is finished, makes it able to become טמא. Yet a second thought cannot undo that status. Only a physical change can. This seems to show that a later thought cannot cancel an earlier thought. That goes against רבי יוחנן's rule that a later statement can cancel an earlier one.

keyTerms.meaning: A change made by an action

phrases.english: Reish Lakish raised an objection to Rabbi Yochanan:
All vessels go down into their טומאה
phrases.notes: 'Go down' means the vessel becomes able to become טמא. 'Come up' means it leaves that status.

phrases.english: through thought,
and they do not come up from their טומאה
except through a change made by an action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses direction: after defending himself, ריש לקיש now attacks רבי יוחנן's position from step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that a statement can cancel a statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Thought gives a vessel its status, but a later thought cannot remove it. Only an action can, which suggests that intentions cannot cancel intentions.
